subject: Reserved capacity commit — start window and ramp schedule (CloudForge)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@cloudforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity commit — initial options and start window

Hi Liam —

Great to chat last week. Per our conversation, I wanted to outline concrete reserved-commit options for CloudForge so you can take them to procurement. This is specific to a Dedicated GPU pool with predictable throughput for your inference workloads. High level: 

- Capacity layout we quoted: 8 x A100-80GB equivalents (single dedicated pool) — provides an estimated steady-state throughput of ~9k tokens/sec for your benchmark prompt mix.
- Commit term options (monthly effective price varies by term): 12-month | 24-month | 36-month.
- Ramp schedule flexibility: we support phased ramps over 1–4 months. You can start with a partial pool and scale to full capacity as traffic grows.
- Start window: we can target a start date as early as 2026-07-15; if you need more lead time we can agree to a delayed start up to 2026-08-15 with limited credits for delayed provisioning.

Pricing/discount guidance (ballpark for discussion):
- 12-month: baseline list rate, small onboarding credit.
- 24-month: ~10% off list (subject to final sizing and commit level).
- 36-month: ~15% off list + eligible for extended SLA uplift.

Two items I want your input on so we can produce a redline-ready SOW: preferred commit term (12/24/36), desired start date window, and the ramp profile (how many GPUs you'd like live each month).

Attaching a draft SOW and a pricing worksheet. If you prefer I can propose two concrete offers (24-month and 36-month) with fixed monthly amounts and explicit ramp milestones.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through.

— Camila
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: CloudForge_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf), reserved_capacity_pricing_v3.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@cloudforge.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: SaaSOps Legal <legal@cloudforge.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity commit — initial options and start window

Camila —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. A few reactions from our side: 

1) Term: CloudForge is leaning toward a 24-month commitment if we can secure a strong ramp and an ability to pause provisioning for a short window if there are delays in our deployment.
2) Start date: target would be 2026-08-01. We need roughly four weeks to finish internal testing and compliance checks. If you can provision earlier that's great, but we need the contract to allow a start window tied to our readiness.
3) Ramp profile: we'd like to start at ~50% of the pool month 1 (4 GPUs), move to 75% month 2, and reach 100% by month 4. Could you confirm how that affects billing/pricing?
4) Discount ask: can Redwood move to 12% off list on the 24-month if we commit to the 8-GPU pool and agree to a 60-day notice for pausing?

Looping in Legal above — they may ask for standard procurement terms and the SOW redline. Also please include the HubSpot deal number on the SOW.

-Liam
Liam O'Connor
Director of Infrastructure, CloudForge
liam.oconnor@cloudforge.com

On Mon, Jun 29, 2026 at 09:12 AM Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Great to chat last week. Per our conversation...

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@cloudforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity commit — initial options and start window

Liam —

Appreciate the clarity. Quick responses inline: 

1) 24-month + pause option: we can do a 24-month term and include a limited pause/resume clause that allows one paused window up to 60 days total across the term (requires 60 days' notice and pro-rated billing during pause). That aligns with your ask.

2) Start date: we can support a flexible start window between 2026-07-15 and 2026-08-15. If provisioning is pushed past 2026-07-31 we will include a one-time onboarding credit to offset the delay (amount varies by final monthly commitment).

3) Ramp and billing: 
- Billing is based on the committed pool size per month. If you run a partial pool (e.g., 4 of 8 GPUs) we will bill the partial-month based on active GPUs used that month at the committed per-GPU rate established in the SOW. 
- We can formalize a 4-month ramp: month 1 = 50% (4 GPUs), month 2 = 75% (6 GPUs), month 3 = 90% (7 GPUs), month 4 = 100% (8 GPUs).

4) Discount counter: for a 24-month term with the ramp and the 60-day pause clause, we can offer 11% off list pricing. Going to 12% would require a firm sign-off on the SOW within 10 business days and a commit to quarterly business reviews (standard). We can also offer 13% for 36 months.

I've updated the pricing worksheet per these parameters and attached it. Dev is copied for sizing confirmation and Jordan will own the onboarding calendar.

If that looks ok to you, I'll put together a redline-ready SOW with the pause clause and DocuSign link.

— Camila

Attachments: reserved_capacity_pricing_v3.xlsx (updated)

From: SaaSOps Legal <legal@cloudforge.com>

Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 09:17:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity commit — initial options and start window

Camila —

Legal here. Please include the following in the SOW/contract evidence so we can expedite review: 
- Clear monthly invoicing amounts per month for the full 24-month term, including the ramp months with per-GPU pricing.
- Explicit definition of "pause": what services are paused, billing during pause, and how re-provisioning will be handled.
- SLA credits tied to sustained latency regressions and failure to meet the baseline throughput guarantee (we will provide our test harness if helpful).

Also please place the HubSpot deal id (CF-2026-017) in the header and send the DocuSign link to legal@cloudforge.com when ready.

Thanks,
— Claire (on behalf of SaaSOps Legal)
